title: The Bhagavata Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: The Purana is ascribed to Vyasa and presents itself as the mature statement of his teaching, but it is a composite work of several hands, most likely composed in south India between the ninth and tenth centuries.
description: The Bhagavata Purana tells the deeds of Vishnu and above all of Krishna: the creation and the cosmic ages, the genealogies of the solar and lunar houses, the dwarf and boar and man-lion avatars, and then, in its tenth book, the childhood, the flute, the dance and the teaching of Krishna in Vrindavan. Its verses are the foundation of Krishna devotion, and its final books set out the yogic and devotional disciplines by which the story is to be entered.
historicalContext: Composed in Sanskrit after the earlier Puranas, the Bhagavata became the scripture of the Bhagavata communities and of the Gaudiya, Vallabha and Bhagavata traditions. Commentaries from Sridhara onward made it a school text, and its tenth book has been translated, retold and sung across India for a thousand years.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit text of all twelve skandhas as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
